--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Notation
theorem add_nfBelow {b} : ∀ {o₁ o₂}, NFBelow o₁ b → NFBelow o₂ b → NFBelow (o₁ + o₂) b
  | 0, _, _, h₂ => h₂
  | oadd e n a, o, h₁, h₂ => by
    have h' := add_nfBelow (h₁.snd.mono <| le_of_lt h₁.lt) h₂
    simp only [oadd_add]; revert h'; cases' a + o with e' n' a' <;> intro h'
    · exact NFBelow.oadd h₁.fst NFBelow.zero h₁.lt
    have : ((e.cmp e').Compares e e') := @cmp_compares _ _ h₁.fst h'.fst
    cases h : cmp e e' <;> dsimp [addAux] <;> simp only [h]
    · exact h'
    · simp only [h] at this
      subst e'
      exact NFBelow.oadd h'.fst h'.snd h'.lt
    · simp only [h] at this
      exact NFBelow.oadd h₁.fst (NF.below_of_lt this ⟨⟨_, h'⟩⟩) h₁.lt

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Notation
/-- A normal form ordinal notation has the form
`ω ^ a₁ * n₁ + ω ^ a₂ * n₂ + ⋯ + ω ^ aₖ * nₖ`
where `a₁ > a₂ > ⋯ > aₖ` and all the `aᵢ` are also in normal form.
We will essentially only be interested in normal form ordinal notations, but to avoid complicating
the algorithms, we define everything over general ordinal notations and only prove correctness with
normal form as an invariant. -/
class NF (o : ONote) : Prop where
  out : Exists (NFBelow o)

/-- Definition of `≤` for congruence relations. -/
@[to_additive "Definition of `≤` for additive congruence relations."]
theorem le_def {c d : Con M} : c ≤ d ↔ ∀ {x y}, c x y → d x y :=
  Iff.rfl

--src: Mathlib.GroupTheory.Congruence.Defs
/-- The smallest congruence relation containing a binary relation `r` is contained in any
    congruence relation containing `r`. -/
@[to_additive addConGen_le "The smallest additive congruence relation containing a binary
relation `r` is contained in any additive congruence relation containing `r`."]
theorem conGen_le {r : M → M → Prop} {c : Con M} (h : ∀ x y, r x y → c x y) :
    conGen r ≤ c := by rw [conGen_eq]; exact sInf_le h

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.Ordinal
theorem toGame_le_iff {a b : Ordinal} : a.toGame ≤ b.toGame ↔ a ≤ b :=
  toPGame_le_iff

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Notation
theorem NFBelow.fst {e n a b} (h : NFBelow (ONote.oadd e n a) b) : NF e := by
  cases' h with _ _ _ _ eb _ h₁ h₂ h₃; exact ⟨⟨_, h₁⟩⟩

--src: Mathlib.Order.Lattice
/-- A `SemilatticeInf` is a meet-semilattice, that is, a partial order
  with a meet (a.k.a. glb / greatest lower bound, inf / infimum) operation
  `⊓` which is the greatest element smaller than both factors. -/
class SemilatticeInf (α : Type u) extends PartialOrder α where
  /-- The binary infimum, used to derive `Min α` -/
  inf : α → α → α
  /-- The infimum is a lower bound on the first argument -/
  protected inf_le_left : ∀ a b : α, inf a b ≤ a
  /-- The infimum is a lower bound on the second argument -/
  protected inf_le_right : ∀ a b : α, inf a b ≤ b
  /-- The infimum is the *greatest* lower bound -/
  protected le_inf : ∀ a b c : α, a ≤ b → a ≤ c → a ≤ inf b c

  obtain ⟨L₂, s₂, h₂⟩ := N₂
  cases nearLitter_litter_eq_of_near (near_of_eq h)

  cases nearLitter_litter_eq_of_near (near_of_eq h)

/--

Otherwise, that value `a` must not satisfy `p`.

theorem Estimator.improveUntilAux_spec (a : Thunk α) (p : α → Bool)
    [Estimator a ε] [WellFoundedGT (range (bound a : ε → α))] (e : ε) (r : Bool) :

    | .error _ => ¬ p a.get

  rw [Estimator.improveUntilAux]
  by_cases h : p (bound a e)
  · simp only [h]; exact h

      simp only [Bool.not_eq_true]
      rw [eq] at h
      exact Bool.bool_eq_false h

  cases nearLitter_litter_eq_of_near (near_of_eq h)

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

/--
In a type `R` with an addition, a zero element and a multiplication, the property of being a sum of
squares is defined by an inductive predicate: `0 : R` is a sum of squares and if `S` is a sum of
squares, then for all `a : R`, `a * a + S` is a sum of squares in `R`.

/-- Given a topological space `X : TopCat` and a type family `T : X → Type`,
a `P : LocalPredicate T` consists of:
* a family of predicates `P.pred`, one for each `U : Opens X`, of the form `(Π x : U, T x) → Prop`
* a proof that if `f : Π x : V, T x` satisfies the predicate on `V : Opens X`, then
  the restriction of `f` to any open subset `U` also satisfies the predicate, and
* a proof that given some `f : Π x : U, T x`,
  if for every `x : U` we can find an open set `x ∈ V ≤ U`
  so that the restriction of `f` to `V` satisfies the predicate,
  then `f` itself satisfies the predicate.

  /-- A local predicate must be local --- provided that it is locally satisfied, it is also globally

  locality :

      (_ : ∀ x : U, ∃ (V : Opens X) (_ : x.1 ∈ V) (i : V ⟶ U),
        pred fun x : V => f (i x : U)), pred f

/-- `CPRankMax N x` means `x` has CP rank at most `N`, that is,
  it can be written as the sum of N holors of rank at most 1. -/

--src: Mathlib.Logic.Relation
@[elab_as_elim]
theorem head_induction_on {P : ∀ a : α, TransGen r a b → Prop} {a : α} (h : TransGen r a b)
    (base : ∀ {a} (h : r a b), P a (single h))
    (ih : ∀ {a c} (h' : r a c) (h : TransGen r c b), P c h → P a (h.head h')) : P a h := by
  induction h with
  | single h => exact base h
  | @tail b c _ hbc h_ih =>
  apply h_ih
  · exact fun h ↦ ih h (single hbc) (base hbc)
  · exact fun hab hbc ↦ ih hab _

--src: Mathlib.Order.Estimator
attribute [local instance] WellFoundedGT.toWellFoundedRelation in
/--
If `Estimator.improveUntil a p e` returns `some e'`, then `bound a e'` satisfies `p`.
Otherwise, that value `a` must not satisfy `p`.
-/
theorem Estimator.improveUntilAux_spec (a : Thunk α) (p : α → Bool)
    [Estimator a ε] [WellFoundedGT (range (bound a : ε → α))] (e : ε) (r : Bool) :
    match Estimator.improveUntilAux a p e r with
    | .error _ => ¬ p a.get
    | .ok e' => p (bound a e') := by
  rw [Estimator.improveUntilAux]
  by_cases h : p (bound a e)
  · simp only [h]; exact h
  · simp only [h]
    match improve a e, improve_spec e with
    | none, eq =>
      simp only [Bool.not_eq_true]
      rw [eq] at h
      exact Bool.bool_eq_false h
    | some e', _ =>
      exact Estimator.improveUntilAux_spec a p e' true
termination_by (⟨_, mem_range_self e⟩ : range (bound a))

theorem tr_respects_aux₁ {k} (o q v) {S : List (Γ k)} {L : ListBlank (∀ k, Option (Γ k))}
    (hL : L.map (proj k) = ListBlank.mk (S.map some).reverse) (n) (H : n ≤ S.length) :

      ⟨some (go k o q), v, (Tape.move Dir.right)^[n] (Tape.mk' ∅ (addBottom L))⟩ := by

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.SumsOfSquares
/--
In a type `R` with an addition, a zero element and a multiplication, the property of being a sum of
squares is defined by an inductive predicate: `0 : R` is a sum of squares and if `S` is a sum of
squares, then for all `a : R`, `a * a + S` is a sum of squares in `R`.
-/
@[mk_iff]
inductive IsSumSq [Add R] [Zero R] : R → Prop
  | zero                              : IsSumSq 0
  | sq_add (a S : R) (pS : IsSumSq S) : IsSumSq (a * a + S)

--src: Mathlib.Topology.Sheaves.LocalPredicate
/-- Given a topological space `X : TopCat` and a type family `T : X → Type`,
a `P : LocalPredicate T` consists of:
* a family of predicates `P.pred`, one for each `U : Opens X`, of the form `(Π x : U, T x) → Prop`
* a proof that if `f : Π x : V, T x` satisfies the predicate on `V : Opens X`, then
  the restriction of `f` to any open subset `U` also satisfies the predicate, and
* a proof that given some `f : Π x : U, T x`,
  if for every `x : U` we can find an open set `x ∈ V ≤ U`
  so that the restriction of `f` to `V` satisfies the predicate,
  then `f` itself satisfies the predicate.
-/
structure LocalPredicate extends PrelocalPredicate T where
  /-- A local predicate must be local --- provided that it is locally satisfied, it is also globally
    satisfied -/
  locality :
    ∀ {U : Opens X} (f : ∀ x : U, T x)
      (_ : ∀ x : U, ∃ (V : Opens X) (_ : x.1 ∈ V) (i : V ⟶ U),
        pred fun x : V => f (i x : U)), pred f

    (H : ∀ a', b ∈ f.fix a' → (∀ a'', Sum.inr a'' ∈ f a' → C a'') → C a') :

  induction ‹Acc _ _›

  /-- The uniformity filter. Once `UniformSpace` is defined, `�� α` (`_root_.uniformity`) becomes the
  normal form. -/
  uniformity : Filter (α × α)
  /-- Every set in the uniformity filter includes the diagonal. -/
  refl : �� idRel ≤ uniformity
  /-- If `s ∈ uniformity`, then `Prod.swap ⁻¹' s ∈ uniformity`. -/
  symm : Tendsto Prod.swap uniformity uniformity

  comp : (uniformity.lift' fun s => s ○ s) ≤ uniformity

/-- A seminorm on a ring `R` is a function `f : R → ℝ` that preserves zero, takes nonnegative
  values, is subadditive and submultiplicative and such that `f (-x) = f x` for all `x ∈ R`. -/

  /-- The property of a `RingSeminorm` that for all `x` and `y` in the ring, the norm of `x * y` is
    less than the norm of `x` times the norm of `y`. -/
  mul_le' : ∀ x y : R, toFun (x * y) ≤ toFun x * toFun y
